business: Moduo: an all-in-one workspace (tasks, notes, calendar, contacts, email), pitched as a client hub for solo service businesses
target: Solo freelancers and consultants (designers, developers, writers, coaches) who juggle several clients across 4+ separate apps
where: Online; mostly US, UK and EU

segments.name: Solo founder of a small service business

behaviours.name: Notion tinkerer
behaviours.how: Has built their own client system in Notion and keeps rebuilding it.

behaviours.name: Tool-stack loyalist
behaviours.how: Pays for Spark, Todoist and Calendly and is fine with how they fit together.

behaviours.name: Subscription trimmer
behaviours.how: Audits their subscriptions every few months and cancels anything they don't use weekly.

behaviours.name: Inbox-as-to-do-list
behaviours.how: Runs their work from email stars and flags; forgets follow-ups.

behaviours.name: Reads every review
behaviours.how: Won't try a new tool without Reddit threads and reviews saying it's stable.

behaviours.name: Paper and calendar
behaviours.how: Uses a paper notebook and Google Calendar; has tried apps and dropped them.

behaviours.name: Early adopter
behaviours.how: Tries new productivity apps on launch day, rarely sticks with one.

objections: All-in-one apps are mediocre at everything; I'd still need my real email client
Moving my clients, notes and tasks over is a weekend I don't have
A new startup could shut down and take my data with it
I already pay for tools that work well enough
No Outlook support is a dealbreaker for some of my clients' threads
I don't want my client email synced to someone else's cloud
$12 a month on top of what I already pay
habits: you have five active clients and two waiting on a proposal
you lost a follow-up email last month and nearly lost the client
you invoice at the end of every month from a spreadsheet
you work from home and a café two days a week
you check email first thing and it decides your day
_notes: Segments and objections draw on .design/tasks-dogfood/research-2026-10/segments.md (1a, 1b) and PRODUCT_BRIEF.md risks. Income ranges and behaviour shares are guesses; correct them before dealing.
